For every surjective $K$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi : \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to B$ there are a finite subset $S \subseteq \iota$ and a $K$-algebra isomorphism $e : B \to \prod_{i \in S} F_i$ such that $e \circ \varphi$ is the coordinate restriction…
nodes.title: Surjections from a finite product of fields are coordinate restrictions up to isomorphism

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\iota$ a finite type, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras, and $B$ a commutative $K$-algebra. If $\varphi : \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to B$ is a surjective $K$-algebra homomorphism, then there is a finite subset $S \subseteq \iota$ such that $B$ is isomorphic as a $K$-algebra to $\prod_{i \in S} F_i$.
nodes.title: A surjective image of a finite product of fields is isomorphic to a subproduct

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, and let $(F_i)_{i \in I}$ and $(G_j)_{j \in J}$ be families of fields that are $K$-algebras, indexed by finite types $I$ and $J$. If $e : \prod_{i \in I} F_i \to \prod_{j \in J} G_j$ is an isomorphism of $K$-algebras, then there is a bijection $\sigma : I \to J$ such that $F_i$ is isomorphic to $G_{\sigma(i)}$ as a $K$-algebra for every $i \in I$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of a finite product of fields up to permutation

For $x \in \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i$, $\varphi(x) = 0$ if and only if for every $i \in \iota$ the coordinate $x_i$ lies in the ideal of $F_i$ generated by the image of $\ker \varphi$ under the $i$-th…
nodes.title: Kernel membership in a finite product of fields is componentwise

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras indexed by a type $\iota$, and $S \subseteq \iota$ a finite subset. An element $x \in \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i$ is sent to $0$ by the coordinate restriction $\prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to \prod_{i \in S} F_i$ if and only if $x_i = 0$ for every $i \in S$.
nodes.title: Kernel of coordinate restriction

An index $i \in \iota$ belongs to the selected indices of $\varphi$ if and only if the ideal of $F_i$ generated by the image of $\ker \varphi$ under the $i$-th projection $\prod_{j \in \iota} F_j \to F_i$ is…
nodes.title: Membership in the selected indices

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras indexed by a type $\iota$, and $S \subseteq \iota$ a finite subset. For $x \in \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i$ and $s \in S$, the $s$-th coordinate of the coordinate restriction of $x$ to $S$ is $x_s$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of a restriction

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras indexed by a type $\iota$, and $S \subseteq \iota$ a finite subset. The coordinate restriction $\prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to \prod_{i \in S} F_i$ is surjective.
nodes.title: Coordinate restriction is surjective

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras indexed by a type $\iota$. For a finite subset $S \subseteq \iota$, the coordinate restriction is the $K$-algebra homomorphism $\prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to \prod_{i \in S} F_i$ sending $(x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ to $(x_i)_{i \in S}$.
nodes.title: Coordinate restriction

nodes.summary: A commutative ring $Q$ is isomorphic to a product $R \times S$ of two nontrivial rings $R$ and $S$ if and only if $Q$ contains an idempotent $e$ with $e \neq 0$ and $e \neq 1$.
nodes.title: Product decompositions and idempotents

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
